the GAD-aluminium hydroxide (GAD-aluminium) immunotherapy was found to be well tolerated and safe.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunotherapies and the use of biomarkers to identify individuals at risk of type 1 diabetes.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of diabetes.
the development and application of novel analytical techniques to the study of chemical and biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GAD-aluminated trial is a well-conducted trial, but that there is a need for more data before any firm conclusions can be drawn.
GAD-alum treatment of children and young adults with type 1diabetes is a safe treatment with a possibly beneficial effect in the long term.
GAD-alum treatment of recent-onset type-1 diabetes is safe and possibly efficacious.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that GAD-alum is safe in children and adolescents with new-onset type  1 diabetes.
we are now able to show that the treatment with GAD-Alum has no adverse effect and that the treatment is well tolerated.

we have demonstrated that GAD-alum is safe, and that it has a potential to preserve insulin production in children and adolescents with new-onset type  1 diabetes, particularly if the treatment is given early after disease onset.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the treatment of type 1 diabetes with GAD-aluminated alum was well tolerated in children and adolescents and that it was safe to give the treatment in a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study.
